Subject: Co-sell / resale aggregator: clarification on metering & rev share

Hi Sean / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the product looked solid and our integrations team is excited about the partnership. Before we start the listing and co-sell paperwork, we need to clarify two operational items that are blocking our procurement and finance teams on our side:

1) Metering ownership for aggregated SKUs: ResaleCloud bundles multiple vendor SKUs into a single line item for customers. For billing/revenue attribution, do you require per-vendor metering events (token usage per model), or can Redwood accept aggregated usage with a mapping file at month-end?

2) Revenue flow and resale commissions: we need to understand whether Redwood will invoice end-customers directly (ResaleCloud as reseller), or whether ResaleCloud invoices and Redwood provides a monthly settlement statement. This affects taxes and our commission schedule.

Attached is a quick SKU map (work-in-progress) and a one-page diagram showing how ResaleCloud intends to meter and resale. Can you confirm the recommended approach and any platform changes required for marketplace listing + co-sell?

Objective: align by end of week so legal and finance can start contracting.

Thanks,
Maya Lin
Partnerships Program Lead
ResaleCloud

Attachment: resalecloud_sku_map_v1.csv (CSV stub, 32 rows)
Attachment: proposed_revenue_flow_diagram.pdf (PDF stub)

Subject: Re: Co-sell / resale aggregator: clarification on metering & rev share

Thanks Maya — appreciate the clear asks and the attachments. Quick responses below; internal next steps included.

Short answers up front:
- Metering: Redwood prefers per-vendor token-level metering for SKU-level attribution whenever possible. That said, we can accept aggregated monthly usage with an approved mapping file as an interim approach if ResaleCloud cannot emit per-request vendor tags.
- Revenue flow: We support both models. Most reseller partners choose a settlement model where ResaleCloud invoices the customer and Redwood issues a monthly settlement/statement and pays a commission. If you prefer direct billing (Redwood invoices), that requires reseller accreditation and tax-form verification.

Internal notes / action items: Ben / Olga — can you confirm technical constraints for accepting aggregated monthly uploads vs. realtime vendor-tagged events? If aggregated, what fields do we require in the mapping file? Also, legal will need to see the proposed settlement cadence (monthly net-30) and sample contract language for reseller commissions.

Maya — can you share a sample month of aggregated usage (scrubbed) so engineering can trial ingesting the CSV? If possible, include a column that maps your bundle line to underlying vendor SKUs and model identifiers.

I'll loop Karthik from alliances to coordinate the co-sell certification once we lock the metering approach. Goal: have a technical plan and legal docs ready to route to finance by next Tuesday.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Partner Manager
Redwood Inference

Sean / team / Maya — adding more detail from the runtime and billing side.

1) Technical: From a serving/runtime perspective we emit token-usage events with the following keys: timestamp, customer_id, model_id, token_count, route_id, and optional metadata tags (e.g., partner_id). For real-time attribution you would need to pass either partner_id or a bundle_id with each request. If ResaleCloud cannot change the request flow, we can accept a monthly CSV with columns: bundle_line_id, underlying_model_id, total_tokens, time_range_start, time_range_end. We'll need checksums and a simple reconciliation ID to ensure records are not double-counted.

2) Ingestion: Our billing pipeline supports a "batch ingest" path for partner-provided monthly files. It runs a validation step (schema and checksum), a reconciliation step (matching to settlement records), and a final accept/flag workflow for anomalies. However, batch ingest currently increases latency for dispute resolution — it typically takes 5-7 business days to reconcile anomalous rows. If you anticipate high dispute volume we strongly recommend per-request tagging.

3) Revenue flow: Redwood's default for marketplace listings is to support Reseller Settlement (partner invoices customer) + Redwood issues monthly settlement statements and pays commissions via ACH net-30. If ResaleCloud prefers Redwood invoicing, we'd need reseller accreditation, W-9/W-8 and a merchant-of-record agreement.

4) Compliance: For co-sell on AWS/GCP marketplaces, we also require evidence of entitlement mapping — a per-customer entitlement token so Marketplace metering matches your internal invoice. That is typically part of the listing checklist.

Proposed next step: Maya, share one anonymized month (CSV) and we will run it through our batch ingest validation by EOD Friday. Olga, Karthik — please review the settlement language below and flag any legal/regulatory redlines.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Partnerships Ops
Redwood Inference
